title: Rust: Function Parameters
description: Explore different parameter passing modes in Rust functions.

steps.title: Pass by Value
steps.description: Write a function `print_value(x: i32)` that prints the value. Call it with `42`. The original variable is moved/copied.
hints: Primitive types like `i32` implement `Copy` so they're copied automatically.
The function takes ownership (or a copy for Copy types).

verification.failureMessage: Call print_value(42) and print the result.

steps.title: Pass by Reference
steps.description: Write a function `print_length(s: &String)` that prints the length of a String. Call it with a String reference.

verification.failureMessage: Print the length of a String using a reference parameter.

steps.title: Mutable Reference
steps.description: Write a function `add_exclamation(s: &mut String)` that appends `"!"` to the string. Call it and print the modified string.

verification.failureMessage: Append '!' using a mutable reference and print the result.

steps.title: Multiple References
steps.description: Write a function `first_two(a: &i32, b: &i32) -> i32` that returns a + b. Call with references to two variables and print.
hints: You can have multiple immutable references at once.
Dereference with `*` to get the value.

verification.failureMessage: Add two numbers via references and print the sum.

steps.title: Slice Parameter
steps.description: Write a function `sum_slice(slice: &[i32]) -> i32` that sums all elements. Call with `&[1, 2, 3, 4, 5]` and print.
hints: A `&[i32]` parameter accepts array slices or Vec references.

verification.failureMessage: Print the sum of 1 to 5 using sum_slice.
